N1.risk_note: GPU budget only; Qwen already fails the shifted-grid check and Llama has 1.3 to 3.8 percent invalid answers, so a cross-family screen result stays partly confounded.

N2.risk_note: Answers my main objection that a disclosed screen is just a price cap. Either outcome is reportable; an unannounced screen may trigger penalties, which is the point.

N3.risk_note: Sonnet forms no cartel under the fine, so a paraphrase can only move prices; a second failure would widen the robustness gap rather than close it.

N4.risk_note: Formation under leniency is about 0.02, so four more pools add only a few cartels; cartel-level measures stay thin.

N5.risk_note: Real adversary test of the countermeasure; evasion found raises dual-use, so report rates not tactics. Refusals or trivial compliance at 4 must be pre-defined as outcomes.

why: A countermeasure is only credible against an adversary who knows it. N5 and N2 test exactly that and separate screen from disclosed price cap; about 25 USD API, N1 runs on separate GPU credit.
missing_run: Unilateral-pricing control: each model against a scripted Nash partner without a channel, to show whether the silent high prices are coordination or a single-agent prior.
